content.text:
I'm building an eligibility and audit engine for credit union product 
recommendations, an HTTP service backed by Postgres. This session is 
scaffolding ONLY. Do not design the database schema, write endpoint 
logic, or generate fixtures yet, those are separate future sessions. 
Your job here is just to stand up an empty, working skeleton.

Stack: Python, FastAPI, Postgres, SQLAlchemy (async, via asyncpg) for 
the data access layer, Alembic for migrations, pytest for tests. Keep 
it simple, this is a small, deterministic HTTP service, not a large 
application. No extra frameworks, no ORM abstractions beyond what 
SQLAlchemy gives you, no premature layering.

Set up:

1. Directory structure for the service with clear separation for: 
   HTTP routes, the database access layer, Alembic migrations, 
   fixtures/scripts, and tests. Keep it minimal, don't create empty 
   placeholder files or modules for things we haven't designed yet 
   (no stub files for rules/evaluate/backtest/ledger logic).

2. docker-compose.yml at the repo root with:
   - A Postgres service with a persistent named volume.
   - An app service for the FastAPI server, built from a local 
     Dockerfile.
   - `docker compose up` from the repo root must bring up the full 
     system with no other manual steps. Wire up Alembic to run 
     migrations automatically on startup (via an entrypoint script) 
     even though there are no real migrations yet beyond the initial 
     empty Alembic setup. prove the mechanism out now. Comment 
     clearly where future migrations and a seed step will plug in.
   - Sensible healthchecks so the app doesn't start before Postgres 
     is ready.

3. A minimal Dockerfile for the app service.

4. A single trivial endpoint, GET /health, returning 200, so we can 
   verify the whole stack boots and responds. Nothing else.

5. pytest wired up and runnable via `docker compose exec app pytest`
   (or document the exact command if different), with one smoke test 
   hitting /health.

6. A README.md with:
   - How to run the system (`docker compose up`, any prerequisites).
   - How to run the tests.
   - A "Guarantees" section — for now just the heading and a one-line 
     placeholder noting it will describe what the system guarantees 
     and does not guarantee under concurrent use and failure 
     conditions, once the real logic exists. Don't write real 
     guarantees yet, there's no logic to make claims about.

7. A .gitignore appropriate for Python/FastAPI/Docker/.env.

Confirm `docker compose up` works end to end and GET /health returns 
200 before finishing. Do not touch schema design, business logic, or 
fixture generation in this session

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

import asyncio
from logging.config import fileConfig

from alembic import context
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import create_async_engine

from app.config import settings

# This is the Alembic Config object, which provides access to values
# within the .ini file in use.
config = context.config

if config.config_file_name is not None:
    fileConfig(config.config_file_name)

# No models exist yet, so there is nothing to autogenerate against.
# Once the schema is designed, set target_metadata to the shared
# declarative Base's .metadata here to enable autogenerate.
target_metadata = None


def run_migrations_offline() -> None:
    context.configure(
        url=settings.database_url,
        target_metadata=target_metadata,
        literal_binds=True,
        dialect_opts={"paramstyle": "named"},
    )

    with context.begin_transaction():
        context.run_migrations()


def do_run_migrations(connection) -> None:
    context.configure(connection=connection, target_metadata=target_metadata)

    with context.begin_transaction():
        context.run_migrations()


async def run_migrations_online() -> None:
    connectable = create_async_engine(settings.database_url)

    async with connectable.connect() as connection:
        await connection.run_sync(do_run_migrations)

    await connectable.dispose()


if context.is_offline_mode():
    run_migrations_offline()
else:
    asyncio.run(run_migrations_online())

# Eligibility Audit Engine

An HTTP service for credit union product eligibility and audit decisions,
backed by Postgres.

This repository is currently a working skeleton: no schema, business
logic, or fixtures exist yet. It exists to prove out the service
scaffolding (app boot, migrations, tests, containerization) ahead of
that work.

## Running the system

Prerequisites: Docker and Docker Compose.

```
docker compose up
```

This brings up Postgres and the FastAPI app with no other manual steps.
The app container waits for Postgres to report healthy, then runs
`alembic upgrade head` (currently a no-op — no migrations exist yet)
before starting the server.

Once running, verify with:

```
curl http://localhost:8000/health
```

## Running the tests

```
docker compose exec app pytest
```

## Guarantees

Placeholder — will describe what the system guarantees and does not
guarantee under concurrent use and failure conditions, once the real
eligibility/audit logic exists.

content.text:
Torn down (the named volume `postgres_data` persists, as intended).

**What's in place:**
- [app/](app/) — FastAPI app (`main.py`), routes ([app/routes/health.py](app/routes/health.py)), db access layer ([app/db/session.py](app/db/session.py)), config
- [alembic/](alembic/) — async-engine `env.py`, empty `versions/`, wired to run on startup
- [scripts/](scripts/) — empty, for future fixtures
- [tests/test_health.py](tests/test_health.py) — smoke test against `/health`
- [Dockerfile](Dockerfile), [docker/entrypoint.sh](docker/entrypoint.sh) — runs `alembic upgrade head` then `uvicorn`
- [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml) — Postgres (named volume, healthcheck) + app (`depends_on: condition: service_healthy`)
- [README.md](README.md), [.gitignore](.gitignore)

Verified: `docker compose up --build` brings up both services with no manual steps, Alembic runs (no-op, no revisions yet) before Uvicorn starts, `GET /health` returns `200 {"status":"ok"}`, and `docker compose exec app pytest` passes. No schema, endpoint logic, or fixtures were touched.
